Flatten an SDMX-ML Generic data document into a data frame

Source: R/oecd_funs.R
dot-sdmx_generic_to_df.Rd

A minimal SDMX-ML 2.1 "Generic" data reader, covering just the structure OECD's SDMX REST API returns for a plain Accept: application/xml request (no dsd or structure-specific negotiation): one <Series> per dimension combination, each with a <SeriesKey> and optional series level <Attributes>, holding one or more <Obs>, each with a single <ObsDimension> (the time period), an <ObsValue> and optional observation level <Attributes>. Elements are matched by local name only, so the result does not depend on which namespace prefix a particular server happens to use.

Usage

.sdmx_generic_to_df(doc)

Arguments

doc

An xml2 document or node, as read by read_xml.

Value

A data frame with one row per observation: a column per SDMX dimension and series/observation attribute, obsTime (the raw period string, e.g. "2021" or "2021-Q1") and obsValue (numeric).

Details

A query that returns many thousands of <Series> (the OECD PDB industry table, for instance, can be well over 100000 series, since it leaves the industry dimension unfiltered) makes this function's own performance matter: each xml2/local-name() XPath search here costs several milliseconds in a document that size, seemingly regardless of how small its own match is, so running one such search per <Series> or <Obs> individually turned such a response into many minutes of parsing (and, with a CI timeout in place, a failed build). Everything below instead runs a handful of XPath searches against the whole document (or, for xml_find_first(), against a whole nodeset at once, which is internally vectorised over every node in it), counts each <Series>'s <Obs> from its already-known child count rather than a further search, and reassembles the result with ordinary vector/data-frame operations - no XPath search is run per-Series or per-Obs at all.
